hero.title: Interview material.
hero.introduction: This page contains the material prepared for the interview. The main section presents a workshop on standing waves and the Kundt tube.

interview.title: Sound Made Visible: Standing Waves in a Kundt Tube
interview.summary: Students create resonances in an air column, observe a standing-wave pattern and use measurements to estimate the speed of sound.
interview.description: A loudspeaker drives the air inside the tube. At resonance, lightweight particles form a repeatable spatial pattern related to the standing wave. A microphone and Phyphox can provide additional measurements along the tube.

facts.label: Question
facts.value: How can sound be made visible?

objectives: Identify resonant frequencies and distinguish successive modes.
Relate pressure and displacement nodes and antinodes to the boundary conditions.
Measure the spacing d between adjacent displacement nodes and use λ = 2d.
Calculate the speed of sound with v = fλ and compare it with a reference value.

sequence.title: Predict
sequence.text: Draw the expected mode and locate its nodes and antinodes before switching on the sound.

sequence.title: Tune
sequence.text: Vary the frequency and identify a clear resonance of the air column.

sequence.title: Observe
sequence.text: Compare the particle pattern or microphone signal with the predicted mode.

sequence.title: Measure
sequence.text: Record the frequency f and the spacing d between adjacent displacement nodes.

sequence.title: Calculate
sequence.text: Use λ = 2d and v = fλ to estimate the speed of sound.
